ordered_diagnoses: Posterior segment inflammation related to SARS-CoV-2

facts.raw_span: severe bilateral pneumonia
recent close contact with a fatal case
No relevant medical history was reported
blurred vision and redness in her right eye
temporary (8-day) pain when mobilizing the globe
Best-corrected visual acuity was +2 logMAR (hand movement) OD
Relative afferent pupil defect
Central scotoma
Positive nasopharyngeal swab RT-PCR for SARS-CoV-2
Negative CSF SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR
Cranial MRI with fine optic nerve cuts (normal results)
Fluorescein Angiography (Day 30): Mild leakage associated with inferior peripapillary hemorrhage

concepts.why: The patient developed optic neuritis, as evidenced by relative afferent pupil defect, central scotoma, and impaired color and contrast vision, in the context of a recent SARS-CoV-2 infection.
The patient had retinal vasculitis, as shown by fluorescein leakage from retinal venules, in the setting of a positive SARS-CoV-2 nasopharyngeal swab RT-PCR.

concepts.preferred_label: Posterior segment inflammation related to SARS-CoV-2
concepts.why: The patient's presentation of blurred vision, redness, and pain when mobilizing the globe, along with findings of central scotoma and relative afferent pupil defect, suggests posterior segment inflammation, which may be related to SARS-CoV-2 infection.
It explains the central scotoma and normal cranial MRI with fine optic nerve cuts.

rationales.F04: The presence of blurred vision and redness in the right eye suggests an inflammatory condition affecting the eye, which could be related to COVID-19-associated optic neuritis or other conditions.
rationales.F06: The severely impaired visual acuity in the right eye indicates a significant impact on the visual pathway, consistent with optic neuritis or severe retinal disease.
rationales.F07: The relative afferent pupil defect is a strong indicator of optic nerve dysfunction, which is consistent with optic neuritis.
rationales.F08: The presence of a central scotoma is a specific visual field defect often associated with optic neuritis or other conditions affecting the optic nerve.
rationales.F09: The positive nasopharyngeal swab RT-PCR for SARS-CoV-2 indicates current infection with SARS-CoV-2, which could be related to the development of COVID-19-associated optic neuritis or retinal vasculitis.
rationales.F12: The fluorescein angiography findings of mild leakage associated with inferior peripapillary hemorrhage are consistent with inflammation of the optic disc and surrounding retina, supporting the diagnosis of optic neuritis or retinal vasculitis.
